summary: Frontend-only e2e test for OmniLocal #1 games-optional + SaaS vertical release. Confirmed 5 of 6 requested flows work, but discovered a CRITICAL runtime crash: whenever the resolved active game becomes null (i.e. after unchecking games-enabled-toggle OR after setting week-plan-0 to 'No game — rest week'), the Quality Customer Maximizer page throws and gets replaced by the 'Something hit a snag.' error boundary. Root cause: Maximizer.js accesses games.active.name unconditionally on lines 227 and 315 (no optional chaining). This blocks the entire UI-driven pause flow (users can never verify 'Games PAUSED' state in the UI, and the games-paused-note / 'Game rules updated' toast are unreachable). All backend paths, /spin public page, SaaS vertical, and copy generalization all work as expected.

ui_bugs.issue: Page crashes to 'Something hit a snag.' error boundary as soon as the resolved active game becomes null. Reproduces two ways: (a) uncheck games-enabled-toggle, or (b) set week-plan-0 to 'No game — rest week'. After the crash, toast 'Game rules updated', games-paused-note, and active-game-title='Paused' are all unreachable. Because settings/schedule are persisted, the crash also persists on reload until the state is fixed via API. Root cause: /app/frontend/src/sections/Maximizer.js line 227 renders `Customers scan → play {games.active.name} on their phone` and line 315 renders `<Overline>{games.active.name}</Overline>` without any null guard, even though games.active is legitimately null when settings.enabled=false or when the current-week schedule is 'none'. Fix: guard both usages (e.g. games.active?.name || 'the active game') OR early-return a paused-state view when !games.active.

integration_issues.issue: Backend does receive PUT /api/maximizer/game-settings {enabled:false} and public /spin correctly renders spin-paused (verified by pausing via API). The UI-side of the flow is broken because Maximizer crashes immediately after the toggle change.

Selecting 'No game — rest week' on week-plan-0 successfully persists the schedule (PUT /api/maximizer/game-plan/week returns 200) but crashes the same page, so the visual confirmation ('active-game-title' becoming 'Paused') can't be seen.

action_items: URGENT: Add null-guard for games.active in Maximizer.js lines 227 & 315 (and audit rest of file for other bare games.active.* accesses). Suggested: replace `games.active.name` with `games.active?.name || 'your active game'`, and consider rendering the 'Send it home with them' QR card + Live QR card in a disabled/skeleton state when games.active is null so owners still see the UI while games are paused.

After fix: re-verify (a) 'Game rules updated' toast appears, (b) games-paused-note visible with red 'Games PAUSED — play page shows check back soon' text, (c) active-game-title shows 'Active game: Paused', (d) same states appear when week-plan-0 = 'No game — rest week'.
critical_code_review_comments: Maximizer.js:227 and Maximizer.js:315 dereference games.active.name without null-check even though the whole games-pausing/rest-week feature is designed to make games.active null. This is the direct cause of the outage.

Because the crash happens inside a top-level error boundary, the owner has no way to recover from the UI (Reload doesn't help — settings are persisted). Owner must either re-toggle via API or wait for support. Consider defensively fetching+guarding, and possibly showing a persistent banner when settings.enabled === false so owners can un-pause even if downstream widgets fail.
Nice: SaaS pacing text is well-written and swap is instant with a toast ('Pacing advisor retuned to your industry'). Industry list order looks intentional.
